A1.justification: Both PDFs describe TensorRL-QAS and provide readable text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices. Existing material can be matched despite appendix renumbering, relocation, and additions.

before.justification: v1 reports original molecular and spin-model simulations, circuit-resource comparisons, training-time measurements, and noise experiments, including appendix results.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds initialization controls, sensitivity studies, extended-action results, and IBMQ-Brisbane-noise evaluations.

M1.justification: The DMRG, Riemannian mapping, and fixed/trainable DDQN framework remains unchanged. Appendix H.6 adds an implemented 20-qubit variant whose action pool includes XX, YY, and ZZ alongside the original rotations and CNOT, a limited procedural extension.

E1.justification: Appendix G adds an IBMQ-Brisbane-specific noise scenario for existing 8-H2O circuits. Molecular and spin-model coverage, including 20-qubit TFIM, was already present in v1. Whether the added evaluation used physical hardware or a Qiskit noise model is ambiguously described.

E2.justification: v2 adds TN-VQE across the four molecular comparisons in Table 1 and a TN-only control without RL in Appendix J. The Heisenberg comparison additionally includes DQAS, GQAS, and GQAS-SSL in Table 6. These substantially extend the comparisons, particularly those testing the contribution of RL.

E3.justification: New evaluation designs include fixed-initialization HEA optimization, one-to-three-layer initialization sweeps, a LiH bond-dimension sweep from 2 to 32, and Brisbane-noise evaluation of one selected compact circuit and two randomly sampled proposals. Existing DDQN hyperparameters, episode limits, and molecular configurations are retained; moving their descriptions into Section 4 does not establish changed settings.

E4.justification: New controls and sensitivity analyses test whether RL improves on TN initialization alone or TN-VQE, how initialization depth and bond dimension affect performance, and whether expanding the action pool alleviates the 20-qubit bottleneck. Appendix G also adds device-specific noise case studies. These address substantive questions beyond v1's existing robustness analyses.

E5.justification: The existing five-initialization averages, standard deviations, and minimum–maximum reporting are retained in the corresponding tables and Figures 3–5. No new repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, significance tests, or uncertainty-estimation procedures are reported.

E6.justification: Existing result rows are largely retained, but v2 adds comparator scores, Brisbane-noise errors, initialization-depth success rates, TN-only errors, and bond-dimension/timing results. Table 7 adds a 20-qubit result of 6.1 × 10^-4 error and 9% refinement with the expanded action pool; the original 6.7 × 10^-4 and 1% result remains. This is an additional configuration, not a same-setting performance gain.

T1.justification: The MPS definitions, overlap objective, Riemannian Adam derivation, noise equations, Hamiltonians, and reward function are substantively unchanged. The Hamiltonian equations are reordered, but no new theorem, proof, or mathematical correction is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract newly makes effectiveness on 20-qubit systems a headline claim, and the conclusion now points to tested action-space expansion rather than only proposing richer gates. The central TN-initialized RL contribution and headline efficiency claims remain substantially unchanged.

C2.justification: New discussions connect deeper-initialization failures to learnability, qualify RL's usefulness as DMRG accuracy increases, and explain DDQN's task-dependent suitability and hardware mitigation overhead. The rewritten nonchemical discussion also becomes less qualified: its order-of-magnitude gate-reduction assertion is not established by Table 6. These materially expand and revise the paper's interpretations and applicability boundaries.

D1.justification: v2 adds a source-code link for all experiments, Qiskit/Brisbane evaluation information, and a suggested hardware-deployment workflow in Appendix C. Most existing hyperparameters, molecular geometries, hardware specifications, and resource tables are retained or relocated rather than newly disclosed.

R1.justification: Targeted additions include QuantumNAS, tensor-network machine learning, GQAS, and BenchRL-QAS references. New Appendix D uses prior RL benchmarking to justify DDQN. The central positioning relative to earlier TN–PQC warm-start approaches remains unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 edits the title and abstract, polishes prose, moves agent specifications into Section 4, and adds explanatory appendix sections, acknowledgments, and an impact statement. The main narrative and substantial portions of the existing appendices remain intact.

P2.justification: The tabular presentation substantially expands with new displays for Brisbane noise, initialization depth, TN-only energies, and bond-dimension scaling, plus expanded molecular and spin-model comparison tables. Existing figures retain their plotted content, while several captions change formatting or placement and tables are reorganized.

improvement.justification: The new TN-only and TN-VQE controls improve assessment of RL's contribution, while initialization and bond-dimension studies expose useful limitations absent from v1's evidence. Code-access information also improves reproducibility documentation. These gains are tempered by ambiguous hardware-versus-noise-model reporting and overstated comparisons, including the gate-reduction claim unsupported by Table 6, supporting a limited net improvement.
